title: The Ghost in the Palace
summary: Terrifying groans and floating lights in the old palace wing terrify guards. Birbal spends the night and catches the 'ghost.'
full_text:
Rumors of a malevolent ghost haunted the northern wing of the Agra palace. Sentries reported eerie green lights floating through the dark corridors and deep, mournful groans echoing from the abandoned basement vaults. Two guards fainted from fright, and the palace servants refused to work after sunset.

Akbar was troubled: 'Birbal, my father built that wing forty years ago. Could an unsettled spirit truly be roaming those halls?'

Birbal smiled: 'Ghosts do not walk on marble floors, Sire, but men with bad intentions certainly do. Let me spend the night in the northern wing with a pot of ink and a lantern.'

At midnight, Birbal sat quietly in the dark corridor. Suddenly, a low, agonizing moan filled the hallway: *Oooooh... beware the dead!*

A pale, glowing figure began gliding toward him from the shadows!

Instead of running, Birbal hurled his open pot of thick black ink directly at the glowing phantom!

*Splat!*

A human voice cursed loudly: 'Curse you! My eyes! My eyes are burning!'

Birbal rushed forward and pinned the 'ghost' to the floor. When guards brought torches, they unmasked an accountant from the royal treasury, dressed in white sheets painted with phosphorus!

Investigation revealed that the accountant had been embezzling gold coins from the old archive room, using the 'ghost' disguise to keep everyone away from his midnight thefts!

The next morning, Akbar had the thief imprisoned and thanked Birbal for proving once again that reason and courage can dispel the darkest fears.
